notes:
Summary: SMB inbound lead using Hosted API for customer support chat + doc search. Early discovery; self-serve onboarding. Primary pain = intermittent high latency and client timeouts during peak traffic in EU and APAC. They are cost-sensitive and prefer to stay on public cloud (no VPC/private).

Key quotes: "Need predictable 95th percentile <300ms for short lookup queries — customers notice lag" (CTO, Liam Park).

Recent findings: - Default client timeout (15s) caused aborted responses when model returned larger token outputs; engineering saw spikes in p95 during EU daytime. - They are on our hosted API region eu-west-1 by default (signup geo-detected). No region pinning in client yet. - Using long prompt templates (system + history + whole doc snippet) — token sizes commonly 800-1,200 tokens for some queries.

Recommendations already shared: - Suggest run of regional latency test script (we sent) to capture p50/p95 across us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1. - Recommend increasing client timeout to 60s for streaming endpoints and use chunked streaming to avoid entire-response timeouts. - Advise shortening prompt preambles: move long context into embeddings + retrieval to reduce tokens per request. - Suggest setting explicit X-Redwood-Region header for consistent routing to nearest low-latency region; recommend eu-west-1 for EU devs but run tests to confirm. - Batching/caching: suggest small batch windows for support use-case (2-4 reqs) to reduce cost but be careful with latency SLOs.

Next steps / action items: - Schedule 60m perf tuning workshop week of 2026-03-15 (owner: Maya). - Customer to run test script and share CSV; we will annotate and recommend optimal region and timeout settings. - We to provide example timeout + streaming client snippet (Node and Python) and quick prompt refactor checklist. - Explore single-week reserved burst capacity if bursts continue (budget approval required).
